O.outcome_detail: faculty members’ perceived ethical risks of AI use in education

cells.quote: Faculty members assessed ethical risks in terms of user-related and algorithm-related forms (See Supplementary Table 7). Under User-Related Ethical Risks, participants pointed to academic integrity violations (“…whether the written thoughts, ideas, and interpretations are really the student’s or if they were written by AI”, A7), lack of ethical oversight (“…some of them were fabricated… if you don’t check this, it will cause a big problem”, A6), and ethical erosion in professional competence (“The work…becomes your signature and identity. you can get an ethics violation”, A12). Under Algorithm-Related Ethical Risks, they highlighted algorithmic manipulation (“AI will give us the answer that is more prominent on the internet… this could cause us to completely disregard the other opinion”, A11), information reliability (“If I’m not an expert in the field, I could take it and use it and teach something wrong”, A10), privacy and data security (“It connects to your e-mail account… it pulls information from your e-mail and creates a portfolio about you,” A5), and algorithmic bias (“The AI they use for assessment may be biased… and the database it was trained on may be biased towards some students,” A1) stand out.
cells.note: The study reports a qualitative thematic contrast between categories of perceived ethical risk, not a manipulated treatment-versus-control comparison or comparative effect.

O.outcome_detail: perceived ethical risks of AI use in higher education

cells.quote: Students also expressed ethical risks in a similar manner, based on users and algorithms (See Supplementary Table 8). Under User-Related Ethical Risks, academic integrity violations (“We’re losing originality. They’re making AI write articles directly, everyone can get high scores, even if they don’t deserve them” , S16) and lack of ethical oversight (“I can’t be sure, I submitted the wrong assignment before” , S18) were mentioned. The sub-theme Algorithm-Related Ethical Risks includes the production of false information (“I can be given wrong information… this misinformation can lead to wrong answers” , S5), algorithmic manipulation (“They collect all the data. Then it comes back to you in a way that is completely consumption-oriented and tailored to you” , S14), privacy and data security (“The collection of this data… does not make me feel safe, ” S2), algorithmic bias (“Some existing sources contain distorted information… it can also draw conclusions from those distorted ones, ” S14), and intellectual property violations (“ AI can easily access information I haven’t acquired… and for me, this is actually information theft, ” S10) were highlighted.
cells.note: The study reports a qualitative similarity between student and faculty perspectives, not a quantified comparative effect; therefore direction is coded as ? rather than 0 or ns.
